correctness.rationale: Exhaustive first-principles verification of all 495 four-subsets gives 369 disconnected complements, cut face vector (12,66,220,495,792,924,768,369), and Alexander-dual vector (12,66,220,126,24). The included 132-pair certificate was replayed from the actual files and each pair tested for a unique proper coface at deletion time, leaving a simply connected two-complex with reduced Euler characteristic 63. Simplicial collapses and Whitehead give the dual wedge of 63 two-spheres. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality and the original full five-skeleton, Hurewicz and Whitehead give the wedge of 63 seven-spheres. Independently computed mod-two boundary ranks (306,462,49,11) agree, but are not used to infer integral conclusions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The special graph is four-regular with abundant triangles and four-cycles and does not satisfy the high-skeleton or high-girth hypotheses of potentially dominating theorems. Existing statements about the cube itself, its line graph’s matching complex, or a rectangular grid are not functorial classifications of its ordinary four-cut complex.

Inspected foundational results and cut-complex family theorems have different graphs or false hypotheses. No equivalent or stronger covering claim was found in actual published-finding corpus searches, the accessible prior ledger or primary full-text inspections. This is an evidence-bounded assessment, not uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The natural cuboctahedral line graph is already classified at ordinary cut thresholds three and five, where both homotopy types are mixed-dimensional. Precisely determining the missing intermediate threshold is a motivated finite homotopy problem. A concrete 132-elementary-collapse certificate yields the complete integral dual and primal sphere-wedge homotopy types, showing a single-degree wedge in between the two known mixed-degree cases. This is stronger than a routine Euler characteristic or field-rank calculation; no family-wide assertion is made.
